title: FLEXIS: FLEXible Frequent Subgraph Mining using Maximal Independent Sets

problem.claim: Frequent Subgraph Mining identifies subgraph patterns occurring above a threshold, but its NP-hardness makes it complex and time-consuming.

gap.claim: Existing generation methods produce redundant candidate patterns, while existing frequency metrics trade computational accuracy against latency.

contributions.claim: A vertex-based merging method reduces redundant candidate patterns and includes pruning mechanisms.
The maximal independent set metric targets lower latency with accuracy close to MIS, controlled by a pattern-overlap parameter.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report an average 10.58× speedup compared with GraMi.
The authors report an average 3× speedup compared with T-FSM.

narrative_sequence.summary: The paper frames Frequent Subgraph Mining as identifying common subgraph patterns above a threshold.
It describes FSM as NP-hard and time-consuming, with a two-step generation and metric process.
Existing generation methods create redundant candidates, while existing metrics impose accuracy or computational-cost tradeoffs.
The paper proposes vertex-based merging, pruning mechanisms, and the mIS metric.
The authors report average speedups over GraMi and T-FSM.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the experimental datasets, workload settings, or baselines beyond GraMi and T-FSM.
The abstract does not report the accuracy measurements or the selected pattern-overlap parameter values.
The abstract does not provide implementation or reproducibility details.
